where: Section 2, paragraph on threshold and Pfa
problem: The chapter defines two detectors (envelope gives |y(T)|, square-law gives |y(T)|²) but then gives only the linear-envelope false-alarm formula Pfa = exp(−VT²/(2σ²)). A student who squares the output may apply this formula to a power value and get the wrong answer.
fix: State that this formula is for the linear envelope detector with VT in volts; for the square-law output the threshold is in V² and Pfa = exp(−VT/(2σ²)).

problem: The node is labelled 'Envelope detector' but its note says 'square law', which contradicts the text where the envelope detector and the square-law detector are two different devices.
fix: Use note 'linear or square law' or 'envelope |y(T)|', consistent with the text.

problem: The edge label is 'peak SNR 2E/N0', which is a performance figure, not the signal travelling on that wire. Students may read it as a voltage or power carried between blocks.
fix: Label the wire with the signal, e.g. 'filtered echo y(t)', and keep the 2E/N0 statement in the text or the caption.

problem: 'For equal pulses the SNR rises about N times' hedges an exact result; with ideal phase coherence and equal amplitudes the rise is exactly N.
fix: Write 'rises exactly N times when the pulses add in phase; phase errors or amplitude fluctuations make the real gain smaller'.

problem: 'the cell under test (CUT) is the cell being tested' is circular and defines nothing for a reader meeting the term first.
fix: Say the CUT is the range cell whose output is being compared with the threshold at that instant.

problem: 'only name how target cross section fluctuates' understates the topic and reads oddly; the models are probability distributions used to compute Pd.
fix: Say the Swerling models describe the statistics of the target cross-section fluctuation (scan-to-scan or pulse-to-pulse) and change the Pd-versus-Pfa curve, not the matched filter.
